text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easier for other developers to use your service. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names that describe the resources they represent, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so clients understand what happened. Write clear documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and possible responses. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these practices saves time and reduces mistakes for everyone involved.
